title: GET /connectors returns only the requesting organization's connectors, scoped further by optional projectId
description: The GET /connectors handler (connector.routes.ts:153+) accepts an optional projectId querystring and is gated by requirePermission(INTEGRATION_HUB_PERMISSIONS.VIEW); the underlying service call is expected to filter by user.organizationIdString.
preconditions: Org A has 3 connectors across 2 projects; Org B has its own separate connectors
steps: As an org A user, call GET /connectors with no projectId
Compare both responses against org B's connector list
expectedResult: The unfiltered call returns exactly org A's 3 connectors; the projectId-filtered call returns only connectors scoped to projectA1; no org B connector ever appears in either response.

title: DELETE /connectors/:id performs a soft delete: status becomes inactive, document is not removed, and AWS sub-accounts are deactivated in the same call
description: deleteConnector() (ConnectorService.ts:504-554) calls integrationRepo.softDelete(), then for AWS connector types also calls awsAccountRepo.deactivateByIntegration(orgId, integrationId) before invalidating Redis cache and writing an audit log entry.
preconditions: An active AWS connector integration with at least one linked AWS sub-account record
steps: Call DELETE /connectors/:id for the AWS integration
Query the integrations collection directly for that _id
Query the AWS accounts collection for accounts linked to that integrationId
expectedResult: The integration document still exists but its status is inactive (not physically removed). All linked AWS accounts are also deactivated. An audit log entry of type 'integration_deactivated' exists for this integrationId.

title: SyncService's updateOAuthTokens writes only the fields present in the refresh response, leaving other credential fields untouched
description: ConnectorConfigRepository.updateOAuthTokens() (ConnectorConfigRepository.ts:334-365) unconditionally sets credentials.accessToken, but only sets refreshToken/expiryDate/scope/tokenType in the $set when they are not undefined — a refresh response lacking a new refreshToken must not null out the existing stored one.
preconditions: An integration with an existing refreshToken stored
steps: Trigger a token refresh where the provider's response includes a new accessToken but omits refreshToken (common for providers that don't rotate refresh tokens)
Inspect the stored credentials document after the update
expectedResult: credentials.accessToken reflects the new value; credentials.refreshToken remains the previously stored value (not cleared/overwritten to undefined/null).

title: POST /sync/:integrationId requires the integration to be in 'active' status before starting a sync
description: SyncService.triggerSync() rejects with 'Integration is not active (current status: "<status>"). Activate the integration first.' when integration.status !== 'active'.
preconditions: An integration in 'inactive' or 'pending' status (not yet completed OAuth, or previously disconnected)
steps: Call POST /sync/:integrationId for an integration whose status is 'inactive'
expectedResult: The request is rejected with an error identifying the current non-active status; no sync job document is created and no queue job is enqueued.

title: Incremental sync passes the correct lastSyncAt cutoff sourced from syncSettings or accountInfo
description: triggerSync() resolves lastSyncAt as integration.syncSettings?.lastSyncAt || integration.accountInfo?.lastSyncAt, and for incremental syncType passes it as an ISO 'since' timestamp to the connector; full syncs must not apply this cutoff.
preconditions: An integration with syncSettings.lastSyncAt set from a prior successful sync
steps: Inspect the job payload/parameters passed to the connector's collect step
Trigger POST /sync/:integrationId with syncType='full' and repeat the inspection
expectedResult: The incremental job's 'since' parameter equals the stored lastSyncAt as an ISO string. The full job has no 'since' cutoff applied, regardless of the stored lastSyncAt.

title: Jira OAuth callback resolves and stores cloudId, jiraBaseUrl, and jiraSiteName from the accessible-resources API without blocking the callback on failure
description: handleOAuthCallback() for integrationType 'jira' fetches https://api.atlassian.com/oauth/token/accessible-resources and, on success, persists credentials.cloudId plus accountInfo.jiraBaseUrl/jiraSiteName/displayName; a fetch failure is caught and logged as non-fatal, the OAuth callback still redirects successfully.
preconditions: A Jira OAuth app configured; ability to simulate the accessible-resources call failing (e.g. network block)
steps: Complete the Jira OAuth connect flow normally and verify cloudId/jiraBaseUrl/jiraSiteName are populated
Repeat the flow with the accessible-resources endpoint simulated as unreachable/erroring
expectedResult: First run: credentials.cloudId and accountInfo.jiraBaseUrl/jiraSiteName/displayName are all populated correctly. Second run: the OAuth callback still completes and redirects to the sync-jobs page (non-fatal failure), but cloudId/site fields remain unset, and this should surface as a connector needing 'complete setup' rather than silently appearing fully healthy.
